claims.text: Compositional complexity, microstructural features, and magnetic anisotropy collectively govern the low-field magnetocaloric response of rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Compositional complexity and microstructural features influence magnetic entropy change.
Compositional complexity, microstructure, and magnetic anisotropy influence heat-exchange kinetics.
Systematically varying composition and microstructure through combinatorial synthesis is the proposed intervention.
Grain size, phase distribution, and lattice strain are the relevant structural mediators.
Competition between magnetic ordering and disordering processes mediates the magnetocaloric response.
Compositional complexity and microstructural features affect magnetic anisotropy.
Optimized compositional complexity and microstructure are expected to produce a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Optimized compositional complexity and microstructure are expected to provide rapid heat exchange.
Optimized compositional complexity and microstructure are expected to provide low hysteresis.
Optimized compositional complexity and microstructure are expected to provide mechanical stability.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys whose composition and microstructure can be tailored by combinatorial synthesis.
A failure of magnetocaloric response and heat-exchange kinetics to correlate with compositional complexity and microstructural features would falsify the hypothesis.
